ic_name: IEEE 1149.1 JTAG TAP Controller (TI SSYA002C primer)
otp_present: functionally — the 32-bit Device Identification register is functionally OTP-equivalent (hard-wired at mask level, read-only via TAP), although IEEE 1149.1 does not call it OTP. There is no fuse-bank or programmable OTP at the JTAG protocol layer.

device_identification_register_content.access: Read-only via IDCODE instruction; parallel-loaded with the hard-wired value in CaptureDR; shifted out on TDO in ShiftDR.

usercode_register_content.access: Read-only via USERCODE instruction; shares the Device Identification register but loads a user-programmed value (e.g. FPGA bitstream version, customer revision).
usercode_register_content.writability: Vendor-defined; in CPLD / FPGA parts the USERCODE register is loaded at configuration time from the bitstream, so it is functionally programmable (not strictly OTP) for those devices.

notes: IEEE 1149.1-1990 mandates only the IR + Bypass + BSR; the Device Identification register is optional but must be 32 bits with bit 0 = 1 when present. There is no protocol-defined OTP / fuse / programmable nonvolatile content. Per-vendor extensions (in-system programming registers, configuration NVM accessed via user-defined data registers) are vendor-specific.
